transcript.name: Élise Moreau
transcript.text: Can I just ask—does anyone here actually want to lead the pitch? Or, if not, what’s the main thing we all want to deliver? I’m worried we’ll lose time if we don’t get clear on those two points.

transcript.name: Lilian Njoroge
transcript.text: I’m not looking to lead, but I can handle the analysis and make sure the numbers are solid. If someone else is comfortable presenting, I’ll support you with the data side. Does that work for the group?

transcript.name: Wei Zhou
transcript.text: Uh, maybe we should look at what each team actually does best before picking who leads. Are we clear on what makes our group different from the other one? I can jot down some points if that helps.

transcript.name: Trang Nguyen
transcript.text: Can we list out what our team actually does better than the other group? Just so we have it clear before picking who leads or how we pitch.

transcript.name: Todd Ramsey
transcript.text: If we’re listing what we do better, I’d say our safety record is stronger and we’ve pulled off upgrades with less downtime than the other team. I’m not looking to lead the pitch, but I can back whoever does with system details. Maybe we focus the pitch there—real numbers, not just promises.

transcript.name: Erik Lundström
transcript.text: We probably need one person to take the lead, otherwise we’ll just spin our wheels. If it helps, I’m willing to coordinate things, but I’d like to know if anyone else feels strongly about taking the front spot first.

transcript.name: Robert Hartmann
transcript.text: Enough. We're not here to pass the buck. I'll lead the pitch. Lilian, your numbers. Todd, highlight our safety and efficiency—facts only. Everyone else, get me what I need, fast. No debate. We move now or we lose.

transcript.name: Rafael Carvalho
transcript.text: Alright, Robert, you’re taking the reins—fair enough. But before we lock it in, quick check: is anyone here feeling uneasy with this plan or the direction? Speak up now, please. I want us all in, not just going along.

transcript.name: Amitesh Iyer
transcript.text: Alright, Robert. If you need anything from the backend side or want code samples, just ping me. I’m good with you leading the pitch.

transcript.name: Lucía Mendoza
transcript.text: I’m okay with Robert leading. Just, if anyone’s not sure, maybe say so now? I’d rather know now than later. Otherwise, let’s get moving.

transcript.name: Trang Nguyen
transcript.text: I’m alright with Robert leading too. Just let me know what data or reports you need from me, and I'll make sure you get them today.

transcript.name: Wei Zhou
transcript.text: I'm alright with Robert leading. If you need me to check anything for compliance or double-check details, just let me know.

transcript.name: Lucía Mendoza
transcript.text: Alright, just let me know what you need from my side, Robert. I’ll be ready if anything comes up.

transcript.name: Rafael Carvalho
transcript.text: Alright, we’re locked in. Thanks for stepping up, Robert, and thanks to everyone else for pitching in so quickly. Let’s keep talking as things come up—don’t hesitate to flag anything if you hit a snag or have an idea. We’re in this together, folks.

transcript.name: Robert Hartmann
transcript.text: If you hit a problem, tell me right away. Otherwise, get to work. I want updates before end of day. No excuses.

transcript.name: Élise Moreau
transcript.text: Just so we're clear—if anyone's unsure or wants to flag something, it's okay to say it, even last minute. Better to catch it now than regret it later.

transcript.name: Todd Ramsey
transcript.text: Robert, just to be sure—when you say highlight safety and efficiency, you want recent data or examples from the last upgrade cycle? I’ll get those ready.

transcript.name: Robert Hartmann
transcript.text: Todd, yes—recent upgrade cycle only. Give me downtime figures, incident rate, and completion times. Nothing from last year. Keep it tight.

transcript.name: Élise Moreau
transcript.text: If anyone hits a roadblock or has second thoughts, just say so—no judgment. Better to catch it now than scramble later.

transcript.name: Rafael Carvalho
transcript.text: Let’s not forget—if something pops up, even if it feels small, say it. Sometimes the best ideas or biggest problems show up last minute. Keep talking, team.
